verses.text: Around that time Jeroboam's son Abijah fell ill.
Jeroboam told his wife, “Please get up and put on a disguise so nobody recognizes you as my wife. Go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, the one who told me I'd become king over these people.
Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey. He'll tell you what will happen to the boy.”
Jeroboam's wife did as he asked and went to Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah had lost his sight in his old age.
But the LORD had told him, “Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son because he's sick. I'll tell you what to say to her. When she comes in, she'll pretend to be someone else.”
When Ahijah heard her footsteps at the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why pretend to be someone else? I've been sent to give you terrible news.
Go tell Jeroboam, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: “I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from David's family and gave it to you. Yet you haven't lived like my servant David, who kept my commands and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
You've done more evil than everyone who came before you. You've made other gods for yourself, cast metal idols, made me angry, and turned your back on me.

So I'll bring disaster on Jeroboam's family. I'll cut off every male of his household in Israel, whether shut in or free. I'll sweep away his family the way someone sweeps away dung until it's all gone.
Dogs will eat anyone from Jeroboam's household who dies in town, and birds will eat anyone who dies out in the fields. The LORD has spoken.”’
Now get up and go home. As soon as you set foot in the city, the boy will die.

All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He'll be the only one in Jeroboam's family to get a burial, because in that household the LORD, the God of Israel, has found something good toward him in this boy.
The LORD will raise up a king over Israel for himself who will cut off Jeroboam's family. That day is here. It's already beginning.

The LORD will strike Israel so it shakes like a reed in water. He'll pull Israel up by the roots from this good land he gave their ancestors and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they made Asherah poles and provoked the LORD to anger.
He'll give Israel up because of the sins Jeroboam committed and led Israel into.”
Jeroboam's wife got up and left for Tirzah. As she reached the threshold of her house, the boy died.
All Israel buried him and mourned for him, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of Jeroboam's acts, his wars and how he ruled, are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jeroboam ruled for twenty-two years. Then he died and joined his ancestors, and his son Nadab became king in his place.

Solomon's son Rehoboam ruled in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king and ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel for his name. His mother was Naamah from Ammon.
Judah did what was evil in the LORD's sight. Their sins stirred up his jealousy more than all their ancestors' sins had.
They built high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
There were also male shrine prostitutes in the land. The people practiced the same detestable things as the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of Israel.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
He carried away the treasures of the LORD's house and the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them. He put them in the care of the guard commanders who watched the entrance to the palace.
Whenever the king went to the LORD's house, the guards carried the shields and then brought them back to the guardroom.
The rest of Rehoboam's acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Rehoboam and Jeroboam were continually at war.
Rehoboam died and joined his ancestors and was buried with them in David's City. His mother was Naamah from Ammon. His son Abijam became king in his place.
